newsitem.title: USA: CBS Radio plots new assault on ad dollars.
newsitem.headline: CBS Radio plots new assault on ad dollars.

text.p: Westinghouse captured the attention of the media world by snatching the CBS television network away from other potential suitors -- but it's the radio division that the company really likes to talk about.

Radio played heavily in Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan's speech at the recent Paine Webber media conference, and CBS Radio Chief Executive Mel Karmazin told a major conference here Friday that the company has big plans for the medium it now dominates.
CBS Radio, now the world's largest radio operator, is about to launch an aggressive new bid to grab advertising dollars from its main rivals in television and newspaper publishing, Karmazin said.

Formed last month through CBS parent Westinghouse Electric Corp.'s merger with Infinity Broadcasting and made possible by deregulation of station ownership, CBS is starting to build its clout. The massive new operation has allocated millions of dollars into a sales effort to attract new big-ticket advertisers in the top 10 U.S. markets.

Karmazin, who appeared here at a conference hosted by the Association of American Advertising Agencies, said the aim of the new initiative would be to raise radio's share of the advertising market. Radio currently takes in 7 percent to 8 percent of the the $160 billion spent each year on advertising.

"Ten percent is the goal that we would like to see. I can't give you a year when we'll get there. But if the advertising pie continues to grow and we could get 10 percent of that pie, I think we would have a good business," the CBS executive told Reuters.

While computer companies, telephone utilities, television broadcasters and cable TV operators battle for in-home audiences, CBS Radio's plan would be to dominate the market for out-of-home advertising.
"Our listening is at an all-time high. Newspapers can't say that about their circulation; television isn't able to say that about its audience," said Karmazin.

CBS Radio has decided to spend $4 million in the top 10 U.S. markets to set up special sales to persuade big-ticket advertisers that radio can now deliver audience numbers once seen only in the television industry.
"... If you add up the audiences of the CBS radio stations in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia -- they are television numbers," he said.
The executive said the new CBS initiative was the direct result of the industry consolidation that followed last year's signing of the U.S. Telecommunications Reform Act.

As part of the new business environment created by the federal legislation, Westinghouse last month completed its merger with Infinity. It was billed as the biggest merger in radio history and created the world's biggest radio company, with 79 radio stations in 17 markets.

Karmazin told the audience of advertisers and ad executives that the new CBS had even more room to grow through acquisitions, saying his group could buy an operation the size of Jacor Communications Inc., which has 43 radio stations, and still meet federal ownership limits.

"Because we're a public company, I must give you the proviso: we're not (buying Jacor). But we could acquire Jacor, and the only thing we would need to do would be to dispose of a radio station in Tampa. We would still be under the ownership limits," he said.

Karmazin said CBS has offered a job to "a major creative director of an agency" to help enhance the creative effort on behalf of radio. "The reason we're doing that is that at the agencies, some of our problems are on the creative floor. That's why radio is not being bought," he said.

CBS could have more surprises up its sleeve, he said. "There's also a proposal out in Los Angeles to a personality who would make the amount of money that our company pays to Don Imus and Howard Stern look insignificant."
